column1: # positive.2: the tests of run_tests.sh's `if section_active positive; then` block, in run order.
# Columns and escapes: see run_cases() in scripts/tests/run_tests.sh. A `suite` row runs
# Bug 031: lazy addrOfLocal promotion inside a branch left the promotion alloca
# uninitialized on the sibling path (if/else, value-if, match). Silent garbage.
# Bug 032: multibyte UTF-8 string literal — .ll global sized by char count with
# codepoint-hex escapes; llvm-as rejected any compiled program containing one.
# Bug 033: discard() value-if desugar phied live aggregates (E0714 reject).
# Bug 034: &&/|| RHS borrow skipped lazy-promotion pre-store (031 class, 3rd
# site). Shape guard; the LOAD-BEARING regression is check_cli_helpers.sh.
# Bug 038: promoted aggregate (String) mutated via &mut in an if-arm had the
# mutation clobbered by the merge's stale snapshot (031 family, 4th site).
# Bug 040: same-named match binders of different scalar types in one fn
# first-match var table raised a false E0500; binders are arm-scoped now.
# Bug 041: post-match merge kept arm binders; a stale Copy `value` poisoned
# a later linear `value`'s consumed state (false E0208). Positive: consumed
# linear binder accepted; negative: a real leak in the same shape still fails.
# Bug 045: nested same-named match binders must SHADOW (alpha-renamed at
# Elab); pre-fix the outer binder read the inner's value on BOTH backends.
# Exit 2i: the nested binder is now renamed (`Option::Some { value: inner }`,
# SCOPE-1@1 refuses the shadow); the outer `value` must still read 5.
# Bug 087: a block-scoped `let` shadowing an outer let/param (if, else,
# value-if, while, for bodies) must vanish when its block closes. Pre-fix the
# interpreter and binary disagreed (1 vs 100, 3 vs 7) and both leaked a loop
# body's shadow; Elab now alpha-renames shadowing lets (x -> x.bN).
# Exit 2i: the shadowing itself is refused (SCOPE-1@1, E0301); the renamed twin
# keeps the lexical answers pinned on the binary, the interpreter and the model.
# Codex review: sibling branches reusing a DEAD name for a promoted aggregate
# (`let mut x: [i32; 1]` in both arms) must each read their own storage; Lower's
# promoted table appended, so the else arm read the then arm's (pre-fix 41).
# Codex round 2: an UNPROMOTED re-declaration of the dead name (immutable array, scalar
# of another type, a declaration after the scope) gets its own binding, never the dead
# Bug 176: a loop body (and a `for` header) is a lexical block in the CHECKER
# too. Pre-fix Check's while/for restored only loop depth and labels, so a body
# `let` shadowing an outer name replaced it for the rest of the function: valid
# code was refused (E0217/E0233/E0220) and a u8 was typed over an i32 holding 300.
# The regress fixture now reuses the body's names in LATER siblings (legal under
# SCOPE-1); the H9 legs below are the leak the rule does not reach.
# Bug 208: a fn-typed local spelled like an imported function is not renamed to it (both
# backends returned 141); binary and --interp must agree on 42.
# Bug 212: the parenthesized heads the diagnostic suggests parse and run; binary and --interp
# Since exit 2i the shadowing trigger itself is SCOPE-1@1: these four are refused
# with E0301 at the inner binding, before the type/mutability errors the bug-176
# fix alone produces. The legal sibling-reuse shapes live in the regress fixture.
# Codex review: a body ending in `while let`, or in an inner `while true` that a
# nested labelled break leaves, terminates; its locals are not exempt from H9.
# train1: `break 'outer` skipping the unconsumed `r` is E0210 first; the _mid
# fixture keeps the H9 property with a labelled break that stays in r's scope.
# Bug 050 / R-0002: a call through a fn-typed LOCAL dispatches to the value the
# local holds, not to a generic function that shares its name. Pre-fix: compiled
# 21 (the identity generic) vs interp 42 — silent wrong code.
# Bug 108: `bool as <int>` widens with zext (it was `trunc i1`, which LLVM
# rejects) at every width; `<int> as bool` never had a meaning and is refused.
# Bug 130: the same refusal for an `Int` source (it was `bitcast i64 to i1`).
# Bug 194: a function with a result type and a reachable end reached llvm-as (`ret void`).
# Bug 195: the else block of a let ... else fell through (the rest of the function was skipped).
# Bug 197: a variant pattern without a field list dropped a non-Copy payload.
# Bug 210: arithmetic on a struct, enum or newtype operand compiled (CoreCheck read every named
# type as a type parameter); TYPE-6 refuses it with E0501.
# Bugs 265-267 and 269: the back end over long functions. Lower kept its variable table in an
# association list (265: n chained `let`s took 21 s to lower at 40000, 111 s at 80000); every branch
# merge visited every binding in scope (266: n `let`s each followed by an `if` or a `match` took
# time cubic in n); SSACleanup settled one link of a chain of constant branches per run of its
# whole pass sequence (267: n such branches took n runs over the whole function); the post-mono
# reference-binding verifier searched its environment list per assignment (269: 7.5 s at 40000
# `let`s with an `if` each, 149 s at 80000). The fixtures pin the behavior each structure must
# keep. The leg below reads the stage times from --emit-trace-json: `lower` (Lower, SSA verification
# and cleanup) and `monomorphize` (which runs the post-mono verifiers). 80000 chained `let`s must
# lower within 8 s, 40000 `let`s each followed by an `if` and 20000 each followed by a `match`
# within 15 s, and the `if` case must monomorphize within 3 s; each retried once with twice the
# budget. The old back end took 111 s, over 300 s and over 300 s to lower, and 7.5 s to
# monomorphize; the new one about 1, 3-6 and 4 s, and 0.5-0.8 s.

# a value `if` and a `match` whose last arm writes `x` and returns, and a `break`): the binary
# returned the diverged arm's value or the program was refused (E0703). Binary = --interp = 42.
# Bug 297: argument order, `&mut` write-back order and a match's merged values on the paths
# whose accumulation changed from appends to cons-and-reverse. The binary returns 42 (as
# `--interp` did when the fixture was written).
# Bug 285: an address taken inside an enum literal's payload was invisible to Lower's
# pre-promotion (statement `if`, value `if`, `match`, `&&`) and to the loop's slot-or-phi choice:
# the binary loaded a never-stored slot or looped forever. Binary = --interp = 42.
# Bug 286: every branch and loop site re-walked its whole region for address-takes, so n nested
# `if`s took n² to lower (depth 8000: 1275 ms). The binary returns 42 (as `--interp` did when the
# fixture was written) for the cases where a site must still walk; then the `lower` stage of a nest
# 8000 deep within 400 ms, retried once at 800 ms (118 ms with the fix on the dev host).
# Bug 287: a deferred call that borrows a local promoted it at the first exit lowered, so the other
# exits (a second `return`, `break`s and a `continue`) read a never-stored slot. The binary returns
# 42 (main's returned 208; `--interp` printed 42 when the fixture was written).
# Bug 301: a borrow of a field or element (`&s.x`, `&q.p.y`, `&w.a[1]`, a method call on a field)
# promotes its root local, and the address-taken walk did not see that root: the root was promoted
# inside the branch that borrows it and the other path read a never-stored slot (main's binary
# returned 249). Binary = --interp = 42; and no root is promoted lazily (`%addr.N`), since every
# borrow in the fixture is inside a branch.
# Bug 302: a loop moved a scalar whose address it takes back into a register at its exit, so a raw
# pointer taken in the loop no longer aliased the local (a write after the loop on either side was
# Bug 303: the value `if` kept the bindings its arms declare after its merge, so a later loop's
# header phi took a loop counter defined on one arm's path and the program was refused (E0708). Every

# Bug 304: a value `if` or `match` written as a comparison operand took the comparison's Bool hint

# Bug 308: a value `if` or `match` passed to a bare generic parameter left the type variable
# uninferred, and Check refused the call (E0220). Binary = --interp = 42.
# Bug 309: a loop in the right operand of `&&` / `||` rebound an aggregate the short-circuit merge
# did not reconcile, and the program was refused (E0703). Binary = --interp = 42.
# Bug 305: a `break`, `continue` or labelled `break` out of a `borrow mut` block lost the writes
# made through its reference (the block wrote a copy back only when it fell through its end).
# OD2 (2026-10-29): the reference is the owner's place. run_ok compares the binary with 42 and the
# interpreter leg below compares --interp with the same value.
# Bug 305, second fixture: raw-pointer, Heap and reference-parameter owners, and early exits from a

# interpreter leg below compares --interp with the same value.
# Bug 307: a call argument `&mut x` is `x`'s place (OD2 part 3), not a copy written back after the
# call, which agreed with the place only under the checker's unproven exclusivity guarantee (OD15(b)).
# A differential fixture of defined programs: run_ok compares the binary with 42 and the interpreter
# Bug 307, second fixture: raw-pointer, Heap and `&mut`-parameter owners of a `&mut` call argument.
# Bug 291: every stage found a struct, enum or newtype by name with a search of the declaration
# lists per use, so n types each used once took n². The fixture's lookups (layout offsets, a Copy
# struct, an enum payload, a newtype) return 42; then a program of 8000 Copy structs, each built
# and read once, must check and elaborate within 150 ms per stage, retried once at 300 ms (dev host:
# check 48 and elaborate 50 ms with the fix, 548 and 343 ms on main).
# Bug 292: each loop's header phis were added by mapping the whole finished-block list, so n nested
# loops took n² to lower (depth 8000: 3011 ms on main, 1084 ms with bug 286's fix). The fixture's
# nested loops (continue, break, an aggregate-valued match in a loop) return 42; then the `lower` stage of
# 8000 nested `while`s within 500 ms, retried once at 900 ms (279 ms with the fix, dev host).
# Bug 228: the interpreter's loops drop each iteration's bindings, so a loop is linear in its
# iteration count (200000 iterations did not finish in 60 s on main). Binary 42; --interp 42 in 20 s.
# Bug 234: the interpreter's calls cost the call-stack depth (its environment's length was walked at
# every call, branch, arm and borrow); a depth-100000 recursion must finish under --interp in 20 s.
# Bug 235: an array element read under --interp walked the whole array; 400000 reads of a
# 10000-element array must finish under --interp in 20 s.
# Bug 027: an array literal compiled natively in time superlinear in its length (EmitSSA searched a
# list of pointer registers per operand; one store per element made a block clang -O2 schedules in
# superlinear time). The fixture compiles within 20 s; so does a generated literal of 2 x 100000
# distinct elements (bug 249: the parser appended explicit elements one by one), which must also
# Bug 248: an element write under --interp copied the whole array (and Vec push/set/pop the whole

# Bug 250: natively, writing an element or field of an aggregate local in a loop rebuilt the whole

column1: # Bug 221: a call's explicit type-argument list of the wrong length was zipped (extras dropped).
# Bug 218: two declarations of one name in a module (MOD-3) were accepted (the first silently won,
# or llvm-as failed); refused with E0299. A type and a value may share a spelling.
# Bug 275: the duplicate-declaration rule searched an association list of the declarations seen so
# far per declaration, and a call found its callee by a search of the module's function names and
# a walk of the signature list, so a module of n functions calling each other took n² to check
# (a 20000-function call chain: 1504 ms). Maps now; every collision is still reported, in the same
# order (error_275_collision_order: `first`, `second`, then `P`), and a generated chain of 20000
# functions each calling the next must check (the `check` stage of --emit-trace-json) within
# 200 ms, retried once at 400 ms (fixed: 77 ms on the dev host).
# Bug 215: an unknown type written in a cast or a type-argument list (backend panic / silent
# acceptance before); Resolve refuses it with E0108.
# Bug 217: Resolve walked only the modules of the top-level list, so a nested submodule (two
# modules deep, a module written after `main`, every `mod x;` file of a project) produced no
# Resolve diagnostics: the cast reached the backend (panic), and other name errors met Check's
# codes. The scope fixture pins that the submodule walk admits what Check and Elab admit.
# One literal run_ok per program: test_ssa.sh scrapes run_ok calls textually, so a loop variable
# in the path would reach it unexpanded.
# Bug 229: Resolve's module scope refused what Check admits: a function hid a same-named enum
# (E0104), a user `enum Option` hid the builtin (E0113), a child's newtype was unknown (E0108);
# each fixture has the top-level and the nested shape.
# Bug 230: a top-level module's known types were program-wide (and held its children's aliases), so
# a cast to another module's alias passed Resolve and the backend panicked; E0108 now. The positive
# control keeps what the environment holds: an imported alias, the import closure, own types and a
# child's newtype. Bug 227's top-level shape (another module's `enum Result` hid the builtin, E0113)
# was fixed by the same change.
# Bug 227's nested half: Core spelled a user `Result` and the builtin alike, and Lower's enum lookup
# by name met the user's (E0602); a user `Result` is now spelled by its module.
# Bug 231: a bound names `Copy`, `Destroy` or a trait of its module (MOD-1, E0125); no bound name
# was resolved, so an undeclared trait compiled and an enclosing module's trait was satisfied by
# spelling in a nested module. The positive control keeps every trait Check gives a module.

column1: # Bug 243: an aliased newtype import binds the alias to the declaration's identity, as a struct's.

# definition's spelling to another declaration, the transported type is respelled to its identity.

# Bug 251: a generic's specialization reads its defining tree's constants, wherever Mono emits it.
# Bug 253: construction and field rights are judged by the declaration's identity, so a child type
# sharing an imported type's spelling grants nothing.
# Bug 262: a child's newtype constructor is bound in its parent only by an import (Check and Elab
# by one definition), and a sibling's or the parent's newtype is not constructed outside it.
# Refused at Check, so the native build and --interp refuse them alike.

# Bug 175 (fails closed): a match whose arms all diverge left its merge block open, so a
# loop around it failed SSA verification (E0708). --interp agreement: the r102 loop.
# Bug 183 (silent): a dereference assignment lowered its destination first (rule 7: the
# right-hand side first). --interp agreement: the r102 loop.
# Bugs 136 and 137 (silent): functional update evaluated its base once per omitted field;
# enum-variant literal fields ran in declaration order. --interp agreement: the r102 loop.
# Bug 190 (silent): an array bound or passed by value aliased its source. --interp: the r102 loop.
